results.snippet: LASU Opens State-Of-The-Art ACEITSE Tier-Three Data Centre to Advance Digital Transformation 22 Jun 2026, 12:16pm 276 Views The Lagos State University, on Thursday, 18th June 2026, officially opened the LASU-ACEITSE Tier-Three Data Centre, a landmark project aimed at strengthening the University's digital infrastructure and advancing its digital transformation agenda. In his welcome address, the Director of Africa Centre of Excellence for Innovative and Transformative (STEM) Education (LASU-ACEITSE), Professor Rasheed SANNI, emphasised the importance of the facility in enhancing the University's capacity for data management, research, digital learning, and information security. The Vice-Chancellor, Distinguished Professor Ibiyemi Ibilola OLATUNJI-BELLO, mni, NPOM, described the project as a significant milestone in Lagos State University's pursuit of excellence and innovation. Distinguished Professor OLATUNJI-BELLO, commended all stakeholders involved in the delivery of the project and reaffirmed the University's commitment to leveraging technology to improve teaching, learning, research, and administrative efficiency. The Vice-Chancellor thereafter performed the ceremonial cutting of the tape and officially declared the facility open, after which members of the University Management inspected the Data Centre. Also speaking at the event, the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Administration) and Director of the Directorate of Information, Communication and Technology (DICT), Professor Oluwatoyin ENIKUOMEHIN, noted that the facility would enhance the University's information technology infrastructure, strengthen data security, and support the delivery of technology-driven services across the institution. The event concluded with a vote of thanks by the Senior Deputy Registrar, Africa Centre of Excellence for Innovative and Transformative (STEM) Education, Mr Michael TADOPEDE, who expressed appreciation to the University Management, project partners, stakeholders, and guests for their contributions to the successful completion and opening of the facility. results.title: Lagos State University - Vice Chancellor
results.snippet: Lagos State University - Vice Chancellor Vice Chancellor Home Vice Chancellor Administration Vice Chancellor Prof. Ayodeji Olawunmi BADEJO, FCASSON, FAPROCON, MNAE Prof. Ayodeji Olawunmi BADEJO, FCASSON, FAPROCON, MNAE Vice Chancellor The Vice-Chancellor is the executive head of the University. The Vice-Chancellor has overall responsibility for the policy and administration of the Lagos State University in line with Section 10(1) of the Lagos State University Law, 2004 which states that the Vice-Chancellor shall exercise the general supervision of the University, in addition to any other functions conferred on him by this Law or otherwise, of directing the activities of the University, and shall to the exclusion of any other person or authority be the Chief Executive and Principal Academic Officer of the University and Ex-Officio Chairman of the Senate. Professor Ayodeji Olawunmi BADEJO, a Professor of Counselling Psychology, was born on 4th August 1962. She has over three decades of sustained academic scholarship, teaching, research, institutional leadership, mentorship and pedagogical innovation. She has built an accomplished career spanning academic teaching, research, administration, professional service and student development. Professor BADEJO obtained her NCE in 1983, followed by a Bachelor of Education (B.Ed.) degree in 1986, a Master of Education (M.Ed.) degree in 1988 and a PhD in Guidance and Counselling in 1998. Her academic career has been marked by a steady progression through the lecturer cadre to the rank of Professor, with significant contributions to Counselling Psychology and higher education. At Lagos State University, Professor BADEJO has served in several strategic academic and administrative capacities at departmental, faculty and university-wide levels. Her leadership responsibilities have included membership of the Lagos State University Governing Council, Chairmanship of the Senate Curriculum Committee, and other key university assignments. As Chairman of the Senate Curriculum Committee, Professor BADEJO contributed significantly to curriculum development and validation, academic planning and the alignment of the University's academic programmes with the requirements of the National Universities Commission (NUC). She also facilitated the development and introduction of new academic programmes. As Dean of the Faculty of Education, she provided academic and administrative leadership that contributed to the advancement of the Faculty. During her tenure, approximately 20 academic staff were promoted to the professorial cadre, while all programmes in the Faculty secured full NUC accreditation. Professor BADEJO has also demonstrated considerable capacity in institutional management, financial stewardship and resource mobilisation. As Chairman of the Lagos State University International School Board, she led initiatives that strengthened the School's financial and operational position. Under her leadership, the School's capital reserves increased from approximately ₦88,000 to ₦121million, while structural financial deficits were eliminated. Her tenure also witnessed significant growth in staff strength and student enrolment, alongside sustained exceptional performance in public examinations. A major hallmark of Professor BADEJO'S academic career is her commitment to doctoral education and mentorship. Between 2012 and 2026, she successfully supervised 23 PhD graduates, earning recognition as a “Mentor of Mentors.” Her supervision record includes a recipient of the 2024 Best PhD Thesis Award, further demonstrating the quality and impact of her doctoral mentorship. Professor BADEJO is a prolific scholar with a substantial body of academic work. She has authored four books, contributed 17 book chapters and published over 60 peer-reviewed journal articles, bringing her total scholarly output to more than 80 major publications. Her research and scholarly engagements have extended beyond Nigeria, with visibility across international academic platforms. Her contributions also extend beyond conventional academic scholarship to innovation and social impact. Among her notable creative contributions is the development of a patented Youth Anthem associated with Lagos State University, reflecting her commitment to youth development and initiatives that connect academic expertise with broader societal needs. Professor BADEJO has further distinguished herself in research ethics and governance. As Chairman of the Lagos State University Research Ethics Committee, she has provided leadership in the ethical review of research protocols and in strengthening the capacity of committee members through professional training and collaboration with relevant national and professional bodies. Her professional service extends beyond Lagos State University. She has held leadership responsibilities within professional counselling organisations and contributed to the advancement of the counselling profession in Nigeria. She is a Fellow of the Counselling Association of Nigeria (CASSON) and a Fellow of the Association of Professional Counsellors in Nigeria (APROCON). She is also a member of professional and scholarly organisations, including the American Psychological Association and the Nigerian Academy of Education. Professor BADEJO'S accomplishments have earned her several national and international recognitions. Among these is the Key to the City of Niagara Falls, New York, conferred in recognition of her professional standing and contributions. She received professional fellowship recognition from CASSON in 2015 and APROCON in 2022. In 2025, she was honoured in Pretoria, South Africa, with a Distinguished Personality Award for excellence in higher education in Africa. Professor Ayodeji Olawunmi BADEJO therefore brings to the office of Vice-Chancellor a distinguished record of academic excellence, research productivity, institutional leadership, curriculum development, financial stewardship, ethical governance, innovation and mentorship. Her more than three decades of service demonstrate a sustained commitment to strengthening educational institutions, advancing scholarship, promoting student development and nurturing the next generation of academics and professionals. With her extensive academic experience, institutional knowledge, administrative competence and record of service, Professor BADEJO was appointed the 10th Substantive Vice-Chancellor of the Lagos State University on Monday, 21th Sep, 2026 succeeding Prof. Ibiyemi Olatunji-Bello whose five-year tenure ended on September 19, 2026. results.snippet: Outgoing Vice-Chancellor, Distinguished Professor Ibiyemi Olatunji-Bello, Congratulates Professor Ayodeji Badejo on Appointment as New LASU Vice-Chancellor 10 Sep 2026, 03:30pm 255 Views The Vice-Chancellor of Lagos State University, Distinguished Professor Ibiyemi Ibilola OLATUNJI-BELLO, mni, NPOM, has congratulated Professor Ayodeji Olawunmi BADEJO on her appointment as the 10th Substantive Vice-Chancellor of the University. She expressed confidence that, given Professor BADEJO’s impressive record of scholarship, extensive experience in university administration and international exposure, she would provide excellent leadership for the University, adding that she was leaving LASU in capable hands. results.title: LASU News - LASU Senate Honours Vice-Chancellor, Distinguished Professor Ibiyemi Olatunji-Bello, at Valedictory Session
results.snippet: LASU Senate Honours Vice-Chancellor, Distinguished Professor Ibiyemi Olatunji-Bello, at Valedictory Session 01 Sep 2026, 05:01pm 233 Views The Senate of Lagos State University (LASU), on Thursday, 27 August 2026, held a valedictory session in honour of the University’s ninth substantive Vice-Chancellor, Distinguished Professor Ibiyemi Ibilola OLATUNJI-BELLO, mni, NPOM, as she approaches the conclusion of her single, five-year tenure. The 332nd Statutory Senate Meeting, held at the Senate Chamber of the Babatunde Raji Fashola Building, LASU Main Campus, Ojo, brought together Principal Officers, members of Senate and other academic leaders to reflect on the Vice-Chancellor’s tenure and the institutional developments recorded under her administration. Opening the proceedings, the Registrar of the University, Mr Emmanuel A. FANU, presented an overview of Distinguished Professor OLATUNJI-BELLO’s tenure and contributions to the University. He recalled that Distinguished Professor OLATUNJI-BELLO was appointed Vice-Chancellor in September 2021 by the Visitor to the University and Governor of Lagos State, upon the recommendation of the 11th Governing Council, and assumed office on Monday, 20 September 2021. Her single non-renewable, five-year tenure will formally end on 19 September 2026. According to the Registrar, Professor OLATUNJI-BELLO presided over 55 statutory Senate meetings, beginning with her inaugural session on 20 October 2021, in addition to several extraordinary meetings held during her tenure. The University also hosted 47 inaugural lectures under her administration, reflecting sustained academic and intellectual engagement across the institution. Professor OLATUNJI-BELLO, mni, NPOM, in her valedictory address, expressed gratitude to God, the Lagos State Government and the University community, while emphasising the role of collective leadership in advancing LASU. She highlighted key achievements of her administration in academic accreditation, research and innovation, infrastructure, financial sustainability, staff and student welfare, including the establishment of LASU as a TETFund Centre of Excellence and the promotion of 127 academic staff to the rank of Professor. She urged Senate to sustain the University’s mission and institutional continuity, stressing that while administrations may change, “LASU must remain.” In the area of academic excellence and accreditation, she cited the systematic accreditation of programmes, strengthened quality assurance processes and the expansion of degree offerings in response to emerging academic and professional demands. Goodwill messages were delivered by several members of Senate, who praised her vision, foresight, courage, motherly approach to leadership, humility, and administrative acumen. Delivering the vote of thanks on behalf of Senate, the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Academic), Professor Oseni Taiwo AFISI, FSPSP, MCIOD, acknowledged the occasion as a celebration of the institutional transformation recorded under Professor OLATUNJI-BELLO’s leadership. “Today, we are not merely marking the conclusion of your tenure as Chairman of Senate; we are celebrating a lasting transformation,” he said. “Under your stewardship, academic programmes were strengthened, research output expanded, and quality assurance institutionalised. You taught us that leadership is service, and you leave Lagos State University significantly stronger, better positioned, and globally respected.” At the close of the proceedings, Senate noted that the 334th Statutory Senate Meeting, scheduled for September 2026, will mark the transition to a new administrative era following the conclusion of the Vice-Chancellor’s tenure on 19 September 2026. Professor OLATUNJI-BELLO leaves Lagos State University with a record of academic development, research and innovation, infrastructure renewal, institutional governance, and staff and student welfare, as the University prepares for the next phase of its leadership. results.title: LASU News - LASU Vice-Chancellor Urges Staff to Enrol in “ILERA EKO” as LASHMA Holds Sensitisation at LASU
results.snippet: LASU Vice-Chancellor Urges Staff to Enrol in “ILERA EKO” as LASHMA Holds Sensitisation at LASU 08 Jul 2026, 08:44am 114 Views The Vice-Chancellor, Lagos State University, Distinguished Professor Ibiyemi OLATUNJI-BELLO, mni, NPOM, has urged staff to prioritise their health and well-being by enrolling in the Lagos State Government’s “Ilera Eko” Health Insurance Scheme. The Vice-Chancellor gave the charge on Thursday, 2nd July 2026, through the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Administration), Professor Oluwatoyin ENUKUOMEHIN, during a sensitisation exercise organised by the Lagos State Health Management Agency (LASHMA) at the Buba Marwa Auditorium, Main Campus, Ojo, Lagos. Describing the scheme as mandatory for all public and civil servants in the state, Professor OLATUNJI-BELLO said the management remains committed to staff welfare. "Health is wealth. I encourage every member of staff to take advantage of Ilera Eko. It is designed to ensure that no one is crippled by sudden medical bills," she said. She commended LASHMA experts for the engagement and lauded the scheme, noting that “Ilera Eko” has been rated the best state health insurance scheme in Nigeria for the third consecutive year. The Team Lead, LASHMA, Dr Lanre GREEN, explained the key details of the scheme to staff. According to him, for public and civil servants, the package covers a family of four: the principal, spouse, and two children under 23 years of age at the time of registration. He added that a token amount is deducted monthly from the salary of the policyholder, while both the University Management and the Lagos State Government pay counterpart contributions monthly. Members of staff who have not enrolled, already have their details sent to LASHMA and they would be issued policy numbers to access the scheme. The session was interactive, with staff asking questions and seeking clarifications on coverage, hospitals, and claims. In his vote of thanks, the Registrar, Mr Emmanuel A. FANU represented by the Deputy Registrar, (Vice-Chancellor’s Office), Dr Lateef SHEKONI appreciated LASHMA for the sensitisation and urged staff to take the enrolment seriously. Other principal officers present included the Bursar, Mr Olabisi YUSUF, and the University Librarian, Dr Omawumi MAKINDE. The Director of Health Services, LASU, Dr Nasir ARIYIBI, Director, Internal Audit, Dr Margareth OGUNKOYA , Special Deputy Registrar/Special Assistant to the Vice-Chancellor, Dr Lateef SALAMI, Chairperson, Nigeria Labour Congress, Lagos, Comrade Funmi SESSI and other officers from LASHMA were in attendance. “Ilera Eko” is the mandatory social health insurance scheme of the Lagos State Government, run by LASHMA. Launched in December 2018, it aims to provide affordable and accessible healthcare for all Lagos residents and achieve Universal Health Coverage by reducing out-of-pocket spending. results.snippet: Internal and External Advertisement for the Post of Vice-Chancellor 15 Jun 2026, 11:14am 444 Views PREAMBLE In consonance with the relevant provisions of the Lagos State University Law 2004 [As amended], the Governing Council hereby invites applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates for the appointment of the 10th substantive Vice- Chancellor of Lagos State University. THE INSTITUTION Lagos State University (LASU) was established in 1983 by the Enabling Law of Lagos State of Nigeria, for the advancement of learning and establishment of academic excellence. The University, which took off with three (3) Faculties - Law and Humanities, Education and Science - has grown to become a citadel of repute with high standards. The University caters for a student population of over 85,000, with enrolment in full- time and part- time programmes at the Diploma, Undergraduate AND Postgraduate Levels. A summary of LASU objectives is given as: to create opportunities for deserving candidates to further their education by providing programmes of studies that will give them not only marketable skills but which will enable them develop their full potential and make them well- rounded scholars and useful members of the society. LASU is also to meet the specific manpower needs of Lagos State for the sustenance of her position as the commercial and industrial hub of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, and the strategic transformation of the industrial capacity of the State and the Nation, as well as undertake any other activities appropriate for a University of the highest standard. Lagos State University was initially conceived as a multi- campus, collegiate AND non-residential University. Today, Lagos State University operates a residential, multi- campus system with three [3] fully owned campuses, having its main campus at Ojo (along the Badagry Expressway) AND other campuses at Epe and Ikeja, while the Lagos State University School of Basic Advanced Studies (LASUSBAS) is located in Badagry. The Ojo Campus houses eight (8) Faculties namely: Arts, Communication and Media Studies, Computing and Information Technology, Education, Law, Science, Management Sciences, and Social Sciences. It also houses five (5) Schools, namely: Library, Archival and Information Science; Creativity, Culture and Tourism Studies; Part- Time Studies; Transport and Logistics; as well as Postgraduate Studies. In addition, the Campus houses the following Centres/Institutes/Directorates: Centre for Environment, Science and Sustainable Development; Centre for General Nigerian Studies; Centre for Planning Studies; Centre for Afro- Brazilian Studies; Centre for Peace and Security Studies; Africa Centre of Excellence for Innovative and Transformative Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) Education; Career Development Centre; Lateef Hussain Institute for Radiation Monitoring and Protection; Open and Distance Learning and Research Institute; Directorate of Skills Development and Entrepreneurship; Directorate of Sandwich Degree Programme; Directorate of Information and Communication Technology; among others. At the Ikeja Campus, there is the Lagos State University College of Medicine with six (6) Faculties namely: Allied Health Sciences, Basic Medical Sciences, Basic Clinical Sciences, Clinical Sciences, Dentistry, and Pharmaceutical Sciences. The Epe campus houses the Faculties of Engineering and Environmental Sciences, the School of Agriculture, the Institute for Organic Agriculture & Green Economy, the Pre-Degree Programme, and an arm of the Sandwich Degree Programme. Lagos State University is reputed for high standards and has maintained a tradition of excellence in various disciplines. Currently, all academic programmes offered in the University are accredited by the National Universities Commission (NUC). Lagos State University boasts of a very vibrant, reputable and successful alumni spread all over the world, who are making outstanding contributions in their chosen fields. THE JOB The Lagos State University Law 2004 (As amended) provides that the Vice- Chancellor shall: - exercise general supervision over the University, in addition to other functions conferred or imposed on him by this Law or any other enactments subject to the approval of the Council; - have a general responsibility to the Council for maintaining and promoting the efficiency and good order of the University; - ensure that the provisions of the Law, Ordinances and Regulations are observed; - be a member of Council; - be the Chairman of the University Senate, which is the highest decision making body for all academic matters (i.e. student admissions, examinations and graduation, establishment of new academic programmes etc.) in the University; - be the Chairman of Congregation; AND - have responsibility for maintaining discipline in the University. The job demands a person who can fully harness financial resources in running the University AND who is able to attract grants/endowments from financing bodies, especially international donor agencies. The candidate should be able to cope adequately with varying needs of staff and students as well as emerging contemporary issues, especially those that are related to social life of students in an increasingly dynamic and urban University. THE POST OF VICE- CHANCELLOR, LAGOS STATE UNIVERSITY The Vice- Chancellor is a Principal Officer, as well as the Chief Executive Officer, Chief Academic Officer AND Chief Image Maker of the University. The Vice- Chancellor should have a deep understanding of the systems and operations of a University as well as provide strategic vision and leadership to sustain Lagos State University as a foremost University in Nigeria. The Vice- Chancellor will have to play a pivotal role in taking Lagos State University to global recognition. THE CANDIDATE It will be the duty of the Vice- Chancellor to maintain and improve upon the very high standard in ALL programmes of the University, such that accreditation granted to academic programmes is sustained. The candidate must be a proven and successful manager of human and material resources. He/ She must meet the criteria expected of a contemporary Vice- Chancellor in a 21st Century University. These criteria include, but not limited to the following: - Possession of PhD OR Doctor of Medicine (MD) Degree AND must have supervised PhD students - Full Professor of several years standing and must have delivered his/her professional inaugural lecture - Minimum of fifteen (15) years continuous university teaching/research experience. - Proven record of visionary and transformational leadership in higher education administration. - Strong commitment to solution-driven research with measurable societal and industrial impact. - Demonstrable capacity to attract local and international research grants, endowments, and development partnerships. - Have innovative revenue generation and sustainable income diversification beyond government subventions. - Must have deep understanding of global trends in university education, innovation, entrepreneurship, and digital transformation - Have capacity to promote industrial harmony through inclusive leadership, dialogue, and conflict resolution. - Show strong commitment to staff development, welfare, motivation, and institutional capacity building. - Have a clear passion for students' welfare, mentorship, employability, and holistic development. - Show evidence of excellent national and international networks with academia, industry, government, alumni, and development agencies. - Demonstrate proven ability to establish strategic collaborations, exchange programmes, and institutional partnerships globally. - Show high level of integrity, transparency, accountability, and prudent financial management. - Demonstrate competence in policy formulation, strategic planning, and effective institutional governance. - Demonstrate a strong advocacy for innovation, commercialisation of research outputs, and university-industry linkage. - Commitment to excellence in teaching, learning, accreditation, and quality assurance standards. - Ability to inspire unity, inclusiveness, diversity, and shared institutional vision among stakeholders. - Strong communication, interpersonal, and public engagement skills. - Capacity to leverage technology, artificial intelligence, and digital systems for efficient university administration. - Evidence of administrative experience and successful management of complex institutions or systems. - Commitment to community development, national relevance, and global competitiveness of the university. - Courage, resilience, and strategic thinking required to navigate contemporary challenges in tertiary education. - Must be in excellent physical and mental health, with verifiable certificates to that effect AGE Must not be above sixty- five (65) years of age on assumption of duty as the 10th substantive Vice- Chancellor, if appointed. TENURE The Vice- Chancellor shall hold office for a SINGLE TERM of five (5) years only on such terms and conditions as may be specified in the letter of appointment. REMUNERATION The remuneration and other conditions of service are as applicable to the post of Vice- Chancellor in Nigerian Universities and as may be determined from time to time by the Government/Governing Council, as appropriate. METHOD OF APPLICATION Candidates should submit Fifteen (15) copies of their application accompanied with detailed recent Curriculum Vitae (CV), providing information on the following: - Full Name - Place and Date of Birth. - Marital Status, Number and Ages of Children. - Academic qualifications with dates (degree with classes; copies of certificates to be enclosed). - University Teaching and Research Experience, University Administrative, Managerial and Leadership Experience with dates. - Academic distinctions viz: grants, awards and scholarships; PhD candidate supervision; recognition by national and international professional bodies/fellowships. - provision of researcher profiles and identifiers for verification; - Membership of Academic AND Professional Bodies. - Scholarly Publications (well referenced and listed in chronological order) - Vision for the University in the next five (5) years (NOT more than 5,000 words or a minimum of 1000 words). - Contribution to University and funds attracted through donations and endowments. - Names, addresses and phone numbers of three (3) referees who should be able to attest to the candidate's standing and abilities academically and managerially, as well as morals, character and integrity. Each referee must be contacted by the applicant to forward, directly to the Registrar, a confidential report, in a properly sealed envelope marked "REFERENCE/POST OF VICE- CHANCELLOR" at the top left hand corner of the envelope, to reach the Registrar on or before the deadline for submission of application. SUBMISSION OF APPLICATION/DEADLINE All applications are to be submitted under CONFIDENTIAL COVER, with the envelope marked "POST OF VICE- CHANCELLOR, LASU" sealed AND addressed to: The Pro- Chancellor AND Chairman, Governing Council, Lagos State University, P. M. B. 0001, LASU Post Office, Lagos- Badagry Expressway, Ojo, Lagos State and submitted to: The Registrar AND Secretary to Council, Registrar's Office, 5th Floor, Babatunde Raji Fashola Senate Building, Lagos State University, Ojo NOT later than six (6) weeks from the date of this publication. SHORTLISTED CANDIDATES Shortlisted candidates will be required to make themselves available for interview before the Joint Committee of Council AND Senate at a DATE that will be duly AND formally conveyed to such candidates in writing. Please note that only candidates who satisfy ALL the above criteria will be shortlisted and contacted for the next stage of the appointment process. results.snippet: Lagos State University - Vice Chancellor Vice Chancellor Home Vice Chancellor Administration Vice Chancellor Prof. Ayodeji Olawunmi BADEJO, FCASSON, FAPROCON, MNAE Prof. Ayodeji Olawunmi BADEJO, FCASSON, FAPROCON, MNAE Vice Chancellor The Vice-Chancellor is the executive head of the University. The Vice-Chancellor has overall responsibility for the policy and administration of the Lagos State University in line with Section 10(1) of the Lagos State University Law, 2004 which states that the Vice-Chancellor shall exercise the general supervision of the University, in addition to any other functions conferred on him by this Law or otherwise, of directing the activities of the University, and shall to the exclusion of any other person or authority be the Chief Executive and Principal Academic Officer of the University and Ex-Officio Chairman of the Senate. Professor Ayodeji Olawunmi BADEJO, a Professor of Counselling Psychology, was born on 4th August 1962. She has over three decades of sustained academic scholarship, teaching, research, institutional leadership, mentorship and pedagogical innovation. She has built an accomplished career spanning academic teaching, research, administration, professional service and student development. Professor BADEJO obtained her NCE in 1983, followed by a Bachelor of Education (B.Ed.) degree in 1986, a Master of Education (M.Ed.) degree in 1988 and a PhD in Guidance and Counselling in 1998. Her academic career has been marked by a steady progression through the lecturer cadre to the rank of Professor, with significant contributions to Counselling Psychology and higher education. At Lagos State University, Professor BADEJO has served in several strategic academic and administrative capacities at departmental, faculty and university-wide levels. Her leadership responsibilities have included membership of the Lagos State University Governing Council, Chairmanship of the Senate Curriculum Committee, and other key university assignments. As Chairman of the Senate Curriculum Committee, Professor BADEJO contributed significantly to curriculum development and validation, academic planning and the alignment of the University's academic programmes with the requirements of the National Universities Commission (NUC). She also facilitated the development and introduction of new academic programmes. As Dean of the Faculty of Education, she provided academic and administrative leadership that contributed to the advancement of the Faculty. During her tenure, approximately 20 academic staff were promoted to the professorial cadre, while all programmes in the Faculty secured full NUC accreditation. Professor BADEJO has also demonstrated considerable capacity in institutional management, financial stewardship and resource mobilisation. As Chairman of the Lagos State University International School Board, she led initiatives that strengthened the School's financial and operational position. Under her leadership, the School's capital reserves increased from approximately ₦88,000 to ₦121million, while structural financial deficits were eliminated. Her tenure also witnessed significant growth in staff strength and student enrolment, alongside sustained exceptional performance in public examinations. A major hallmark of Professor BADEJO'S academic career is her commitment to doctoral education and mentorship. Between 2012 and 2026, she successfully supervised 23 PhD graduates, earning recognition as a “Mentor of Mentors.” Her supervision record includes a recipient of the 2024 Best PhD Thesis Award, further demonstrating the quality and impact of her doctoral mentorship. Professor BADEJO is a prolific scholar with a substantial body of academic work. She has authored four books, contributed 17 book chapters and published over 60 peer-reviewed journal articles, bringing her total scholarly output to more than 80 major publications. Her research and scholarly engagements have extended beyond Nigeria, with visibility across international academic platforms. Her contributions also extend beyond conventional academic scholarship to innovation and social impact. Among her notable creative contributions is the development of a patented Youth Anthem associated with Lagos State University, reflecting her commitment to youth development and initiatives that connect academic expertise with broader societal needs. Professor BADEJO has further distinguished herself in research ethics and governance. As Chairman of the Lagos State University Research Ethics Committee, she has provided leadership in the ethical review of research protocols and in strengthening the capacity of committee members through professional training and collaboration with relevant national and professional bodies. Her professional service extends beyond Lagos State University. She has held leadership responsibilities within professional counselling organisations and contributed to the advancement of the counselling profession in Nigeria. She is a Fellow of the Counselling Association of Nigeria (CASSON) and a Fellow of the Association of Professional Counsellors in Nigeria (APROCON). She is also a member of professional and scholarly organisations, including the American Psychological Association and the Nigerian Academy of Education. Professor BADEJO'S accomplishments have earned her several national and international recognitions. Among these is the Key to the City of Niagara Falls, New York, conferred in recognition of her professional standing and contributions. She received professional fellowship recognition from CASSON in 2015 and APROCON in 2022. In 2025, she was honoured in Pretoria, South Africa, with a Distinguished Personality Award for excellence in higher education in Africa. Professor Ayodeji Olawunmi BADEJO therefore brings to the office of Vice-Chancellor a distinguished record of academic excellence, research productivity, institutional leadership, curriculum development, financial stewardship, ethical governance, innovation and mentorship. Her more than three decades of service demonstrate a sustained commitment to strengthening educational institutions, advancing scholarship, promoting student development and nurturing the next generation of academics and professionals. With her extensive academic experience, institutional knowledge, administrative competence and record of service, Professor BADEJO was appointed the 10th Substantive Vice-Chancellor of the Lagos State University on Monday, 21th Sep, 2026 succeeding Prof. Ibiyemi Olatunji-Bello whose five-year tenure ended on September 19, 2026. results.title: LASU News - Special Window of LASU 2026/2027 Indigeneship Verification Exercise for LASU JUPEB and Other Direct Entry Candidates
results.snippet: Special Window of LASU 2026/2027 Indigeneship Verification Exercise for LASU JUPEB and Other Direct Entry Candidates 12 Oct 2026, 10:20am 687 Views The Vice-Chancellor has graciously approved the re-opening of 2026/2027 Lagos State University Independent Indigeneship Verification Exercise (IIVE) portal for JUPEB and other Direct Entry (DE) candidates only. For emphasis, this window of Indigeneship Verification Exercise (IVE) is for JUPEB and other Direct Entry candidates that chose LASU as their First Choice Institution during the 2026 JAMB registration, and are indigenes of Lagos State but yet have not yet participated in the Indigeneship Verification Exercise. Time Frame: This special window will run from Monday, 12th October 2026 to Friday, 16th October 2026. About the LASU Indigeneship Verification Exercise The Indigeneship Verification Exercise is a mandatory pre-admission screening conducted by Lagos State University for all candidates of Lagos State origin. It is administered by the Independent Indigeneship Verification Committee (IIVC) and is a prerequisite for being considered for admission. No Lagos State indigene candidate can be offered admission without first being cleared through this process. Screening Venue for all Lagos State Divisions: New TETFund Building, Faculty of Arts The affected JUPEB and other Direct Entry candidates should attend the verification exercise at the stipulated venue. They can also contact the LASU Admissions Office for necessary guidance. How to Apply: Step by Step Step 1: Confirm Your Eligibility Only JUPEB 2026 graduates and other DE candidates who are indigenes of Lagos State are eligible to participate. Step 2: Make Payment Online Visit the official LASU portal and make your payment through the University’s official online payment link. Do not pay through any individual, agent, or unofficial account. The University has issued a clear disclaimer: any candidate who pays through an unauthorised channel does so entirely at their own risk. Step 3: Complete Online Registration After payment, complete your registration on the portal. Keep your payment receipt and registration confirmation — you will need both for the physical screening exercise. Step 4: Attend the Physical Screening Attend the screening at the venue assigned to your division. Come with all original documents, including your JAMB DE slip, evidence of Lagos State indigeneship, and your payment/registration confirmation. Step 5: Receive Your Clearance Certificate Candidates who are successfully verified will be issued an LASU Indigeneship Clearance Certificate. This certificate is required before any admission offer can be processed. It does not guarantee admission. results.title: LASU News - LASU Retains No. 1 Position in West Africa, Makes Historic Leap to 493rd Globally in UI Greenmetric 2026
results.snippet: LASU Retains No. 1 Position in West Africa, Makes Historic Leap to 493rd Globally in UI Greenmetric 2026 26 Sep 2026, 07:29am 898 Views ‎Lagos State University (LASU) has once again retained its leadership in sustainable university development, retaining its position as the Overall Best University in West Africa in the 2026 UI GreenMetric Sustainable University Rankings. ‎ ‎ The latest result, announced at the UI GreenMetric Sustainable University Rankings 2026 Results and Awards Ceremony in Baku, Azerbaijan, places LASU 493rd globally among 2,016 institutions across 110 countries, representing a remarkable advancement from its 760th position in the 2025 ranking. ‎ ‎The latest feat extends LASU's remarkable run at the summit of sustainable university rankings in West Africa. Since the University joined the UI GreenMetric ranking in 2022, LASU has consistently emerged as the No. 1 university in West Africa, retaining the position for the fifth consecutive ranking cycle (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, and 2026). ‎ ‎Beyond its sustained regional leadership, the 2026 result represents a significant leap in LASU's global sustainability standing. The University has progressed from 799th globally in 2024, to 760th in 2025, and now to 493rd in 2026, an advancement of 267 places in just one year and 306 places from its 2024 position. ‎ ‎The 2026 UI GreenMetric ranking assesses universities on sustainability performance across key areas including Setting and Infrastructure, Energy and Climate Change, Waste, Water, Transportation, Education, and Governance and Digitalisation. LASU's 2026 performance reflects the University's continuing institutional commitment to embedding sustainability, environmental responsibility, and innovative practices across its operations. ‎ ‎In August 2026, LASU also received international recognition for its contribution to the UI GreenMetric network, with its National and Regional Coordinatorship renewed, alongside its elevation to Co-Chairmanship of key sessions at UI GreenMetric international events for the 2026/2027 academic session. ‎ ‎The latest achievement reflects the collective efforts of the University Management, staff, students and the various units and committees contributing to LASU's sustainability agenda. It further reinforces the University's growing profile as a leading institution not only in academic excellence, but also in sustainable development, innovation, responsible governance, and institutional transformation. ‎ ‎The Vice-Chancellor, Professor Ayodeji Olawunmi BADEJO, FCASSON, FAPROCON, MNAE, congratulates the entire LASU community on this remarkable achievement and commends all those whose commitment and contributions continue to advance the University's sustainability agenda. ‎ ‎As LASU continues to build on the achievements of previous administrations, the latest UI GreenMetric result provides yet another indication of the University's steady progress and its ambition to remain a leading institution in Africa and on the global higher education landscape. ‎ ‎We are LASU, We are Great! Tag: West Africa No. 1 Position UI Greenmetric 2026 Share on: Share
